title: Copilot Credits: the shared meter for usage-based AI billing
summary: The page passes: Microsoft's documentation supports its billing, licensing, spending controls and reporting statements. The flagged allocation endpoint and agent-limit navigation are supported, and independent searches found no documented operation for the two API gaps.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Switching environments; controls[1].note
claims.claim: A covering resource-based policy replaces the environment's Power Platform capacity allocation and linked billing plan.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.claim: Selecting All environments makes that transition for every tenant environment.
claims.quote: Selecting All environments makes this change for every environment in the tenant.

claims.claim: Covering Microsoft 365 spending controls take precedence over Power Platform controls.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.claim: Resource-based policies take precedence over identity-based policies.
claims.quote: Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.claim: Overlapping spending-policy limits are not combined.
claims.quote: Spending limits from overlapping policies aren't combined.

claims.claim: An agent reaching its resource-policy limit does not fall back to the user's identity-based policy.
claims.quote: If the agent reaches that limit, usage does not fall back to the user's identity-based policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 resource-based policies do not cover AI Builder features or their credits, and Microsoft advises against moving resources using them.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume. ... Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Agent limits; controls[5].note

claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit

claims.claim: An agent's monthly limit does not stop the agent flows it calls.
claims.quote: An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls.

claims.claim: New agent flow runs are blocked only when the environment has no available Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately, and new agent flow runs are blocked only when the environment has no Copilot Credits available.

claims.quote: Credits allocated to environments in the Power Platform admin center reduce the credits available for other services in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The dashboard-comparison page documents blocked requests when limits or credit sources are exhausted and pay-as-you-go is unavailable.
claims.quote: No available Prepaid Capacity pack credits or Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plans (P3) commit units, and pay-as-you-go isn't enabled | Requests are blocked when limits or available credit sources are exhausted.

claims.claim: Standard-harness prepaid custom-agent documentation allows an overage grace period.
claims.quote: Microsoft allows some level of overage consumption, similar to a grace period, to avoid blocking business processes.

claims.claim: That prepaid custom-agent enforcement is triggered at 125% of tenant prepaid capacity.
claims.quote: Applies to all tenants operating under the Copilot Studio prepaid capacity model for custom agent usage (conversational and autonomously triggered). ... Enforcement is triggered when a tenant reaches 125% of their prepaid capacity.
